Good morning, Roberto. I am Karen Doyle, the buyer for the Midwest region. Thank you for making the time.
Good morning, Karen. Thank you for the call. Could you tell me what you are looking for this year?
We are looking for a new supplier for our private label line. Two products, to start.
We can do that. Would you be able to send me the specification, so I can prepare a quote?
Of course. And what is your usual lead time from Brazil?
Thirty days to the port, and about eighteen days at sea after that. Could we start with a trial order? It is faster, and it is safer for both of us.
I like that. And what are your terms for a first order? Is a discount possible on a small quantity?
I am afraid we cannot give our best price on a small quantity, but we can offer better payment terms. Could I send you the quote by Friday?
Friday works. Send it to me and I will read it before our next call. If the numbers work, we can place the order in July.

Hi, this is Dana calling from Northline Foods. I work with Karen Doyle, and she asked me to reach you before Thursday. Two quick things. First, the meeting moved from ten to eleven, same day, same link, so please do not join at ten. Second, she would like the quote before the call, not during it. She reads everything the night before, and she says the meeting is much shorter when she can arrive with her questions ready. If you can, put the lead time and the payment terms on the first page. She never reads the second page before a first call. And if a trial order is possible, please write the minimum quantity, because that is the first thing our finance team is going to ask. Thank you, and talk to you Thursday.

I have been a buyer for nineteen years, and I can tell you what really happens in the first ten minutes of a first call. I am not deciding whether your product is good. I am deciding whether you are easy to work with. Three things tell me that. The first one is whether you answer the question I asked, or the question you prepared. If I ask about lead time and you tell me about your factory, I write one word in my notes, and it is not a good word. The second one is whether your numbers change. If the price on the call is not the price in the quote, that is the end of it for me. And the third one is whether you can say no. A supplier who says yes to everything in the first call says no to everything in month three. Tell me what you cannot do. I will trust the rest of it much more.
